title: The Curious Case of the Default Settings: Evaluating Default Performance of Variational Inference Software
abstract: We systematically evaluate a suite of off-the-shelf variational inference (VI) software packages from the perspective of a standard practitioner. Using simple analytic benchmark models, we assess the accuracy and stability of the default VI settings in PyMC, NumPyro, and TensorFlow Probability. Unlike previous research focusing on methodological advances, our evaluation emphasizes software implementation and the default configurations that typical users encounter. Our results show that default settings can yield biased approximations of posterior summaries even for simple one-dimensional conjugate models, controls of initialization and transformations differ between software implementations, and relying on defaults may yield silent failures or poor approximations.
